Ask the apprentice: does JQ1 engage BRD4?

Two ways to answer this. f - the one-shot model. A frozen GNN (MOTIVE) maps (gene, compound) -> one scalar. All the compute was spent at training; you get a number with no account of itself. A - the apprentice. After the question arrives, an agent goes out and gathers evidence: it pulls the morphology, asks whether the compound is even active, checks an orthogonal dependency assay, reads the literature, and lays out what each piece says - then commits to a verdict you can audit and proposes what to measure next. This notebook is A's worktable for one pair: it carries its own evidence streams and works the question top to bottom. The bottom line, told up front: the predictive evidence comes back thin, and the value is that the apprentice says exactly which part is thin and why - which the scalar cannot.

1. Find the pair in the data

JQ1 resolves to JCP2022_017085; BRD4 has both an ORF (over-expression) and a CRISPR (knockout) profile in JUMP. The compound profile is 5 wells from source_7 (5 wells). All from source 7 - JUMP's documented batch-effect source, so any cross-source comparison below is on thin ice.

2. Is the compound even doing anything?

Before trusting a weak connectivity, rule out a dead profile. JQ1 is morphologically active - activity mAP 1.00 (corrected p 0.0001). So whatever the connectivity says, it is a real measurement of a real phenotype, not noise.

3. Does the compound's morphology connect to the gene's?

Cosine of JQ1 against BRD4 in the shared feature space: +0.035 vs the ORF (over-expression) and +0.072 vs the CRISPR (knockout). An inhibitor should anti-correlate over-expression and correlate knockout; here the sign pattern is NOT inhibitor-consistent. And BRD4 sits at only the 49.6th percentile of this compound's connectivity against all genes - middle of the pack. Morphology alone does not carry this pair.

4. An orthogonal check: DepMap dependency deconvolution

Independent of morphology: do the cell lines whose growth depends on BRD4 (Chronos knockout) also respond to JQ1 (PRISM sensitivity)? Pearson r = +0.071 across 383 cell lines - weak. The reason is legible: BRD4's Chronos dependency is mean -1.01, std 0.32 - it is common-essential (nearly every line needs it), so there is almost no line-to-line variation for a correlation to grip. This assay is structurally blind here; that is not evidence against the pair.

5. What does the literature say?

JQ1 is a selective BET bromodomain inhibitor; binds BRD4 BD1/BD2 at Kd ~50/90 nM (Filippakopoulos et al., Nature 2010) - a real, high-affinity interaction. So the ground truth is that this interaction is real and high-affinity - even though the two predictive streams above could not confirm it. This row is marked leaky = yes (prior knowledge), so the verdict below is not allowed to count it - it is here to calibrate, not to decide.

6. The one-shot baseline, for contrast

What f hands you for this pair: compound AP 0.668 (degree 3); gene AP 0.341 (degree 6). Two numbers, and no account of any of the six steps above - not the source-7 caveat, not the activity, not the common-essentiality. That opacity is the thing the apprentice replaces.

data.text/markdown:
The apprentice's answer

Verdict: not supported by predictive evidence (confidence low, score 0.0 of 3, predictive evidence only). It rests on:
  • CAVEAT: compound profile is source-7-only (batch-effect source)
  • morphology sign pattern not inhibitor-consistent
  • gene at 50th pct of connectivity (unremarkable)
  • DepMap correlation weak (r=+0.07) - gene is common-essential, so this assay has little differential signal to deconvolve (not evidence against the pair)
Reconciling it. The predictive streams are thin, yet the literature says the interaction is real. The apprentice does not paper over that - it names the two reasons the data is quiet: JQ1's JUMP profile is source-7-only (a batch-effect source), and BRD4 is common-essential, which blinds the DepMap deconvolution. Active compound + blinded assays + a real but unconfirmed interaction is a diagnosis, not a dead end. Score the reasoning, not the scalar. What to measure next.
  • Re-acquire JQ1's Cell Painting profile in one or two non-source-7 labs. If the weak ORF/CRISPR connectivity persists across sources, it is real biology; if it strengthens, the source-7 batch effect was hiding the signal.
  • Profile a BRD4 degrader (e.g. dBET6) alongside the CRISPR knockout. A degrader gives a cleaner loss-of-function morphology, so the inhibitor sign test (anti-correlate over-expression, correlate knockdown) actually becomes decisive for this pair.
